prompts: Create {WS}/scene/index.html: a single-file 3D scene with three.js 0.170.0 loaded from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js (an import map is fine), in low poly or voxel style, showing the classic view of Mount Fuji with the Chureito pagoda (red, five tiers) and cherry trees in bloom in the foreground, with an atmospheric sky (dusk or haze). All geometry must be procedural (no external models or textures). The camera must frame the composition on load; include a subtle animation. This is your ONLY request: there will be no second turn and no answers to questions. Deliver the complete, working final file. Work only inside {WS}.
answers:
Done. `scene/index.html` is complete and verified in a live browser render (screenshot above, `window.__sceneReady` confirmed, no load errors).

**Goal:** single-file procedural 3D scene: Mount Fuji, red five-tier Chureito pagoda, blooming cherry trees, dusk sky.

**What's in the file** (all geometry/materials procedural, three.js 0.170.0 via import map from the jsdelivr CDN):
- **Fuji:** displaced low-poly cone with radial ridges, cratered apex, per-face vertex-colored snow line with warm sun-kissed tint on the right flank.
- **Pagoda:** five tiers (red bodies, white bands, dark pyramidal roofs, finial with rings), on a stone base, clearly framed left of center.
- **Cherry trees:** recursive branch trunks with icosahedron blossom canopies, framing left/right.
- **Dusk atmosphere:** shader-gradient sky dome (indigo → rose → orange), low sun glow sprite (canvas radial gradient), drifting low-poly clouds, haze bands, warm fog, faint zenith stars.
- **Framing:** camera fixed on load with pagoda left, Fuji center-right, sun glow right.
- **Subtle animation:** slow camera drift, swaying canopies, drifting clouds/haze, ~260 instanced falling petals.

**Verification:** rendered twice via `file://` in Chromium; second pass confirmed the fixes (pagoda unblocked and reading red, brighter blossoms, no hard horizon edge). No external models or textures used.
